cta.text: What I check, and what I never do

props.heading: I won't touch a site that isn't yours

body.paragraph: A check on someone else's site is not okay, even when it's meant kindly. So I'll only ever look at a site you've proved is yours, and I'll show the report to you and no one else.

A short page, in plain words: here's the door, here's how I'd get in, here's how to shut it. The most important first. No jargon you have to look up, no pile of red marks, no pressure to buy anything.
Coming. It isn't built yet, and I won't give you a date until it is.
People who look after a small website and would like a friendly second pair of eyes: a shop, a studio, a membership site, a newsletter. If you can say "I'd rather know," I'm for you.

props.heading: I check the doors so you can stop wondering about them.

pages.title: What I check, and what I will never do
pages.description: The check is coming. I won't give you a date until it's real. This is the promise I'm making before it exists, so you can hold me to it.

props.heading: What I check, and what I will never do
props.lead: The check is coming. I won't give you a date until it's real. This is the promise I'm making before it exists, so you can hold me to it.

body.subheading: 1. I only come in when you open the door.
body.paragraph: First you prove the site is yours. Put a small file on your website, or add one line to your home page, the way Google asks. I give you the exact words, and I look for them on your site itself, at the start and again at the end. You sign in with Key first. A web address someone just types in is never enough: not mine, not a friend's, not a competitor's.

body.subheading: 2. I only do safe, quiet things.
body.paragraph: I read what any visitor could read. I don't try passwords, guess at your login, or fire anything at your site to see if it breaks.
I read your robots.txt (the note that tells search engines to keep out), but I don't treat it as a stop sign, because you asked me to look.
One request at a time, about one a second. A check stops at 80 requests or five minutes, whichever comes first. Your site won't feel it.
Every request carries a name that says it's the Super Intelligent Hacker, so your web host can see it's me. You can tell me to stay away by adding one line to a file on your site.
Only the owner who proved the site can open it. I don't share it, I don't sell it, I don't show it to anyone else.

body.subheading: 6. I never keep your passwords or keys.
body.paragraph: A secret key is a password-like code that lets one service talk to another. If I find one sitting in a public page, I'll tell you where, and show only how it begins (like "sk_") and how long it is. I never store the rest.
No red alarm, no "you've been hacked", no countdown, no pushing you to buy anything. Just the door and how to shut it.
The first check will look at these, only from the outside and only the quiet way. None of it is running yet.

points.point: Your site's padlock (its secure connection): that it's there and set up well.
The safety settings your site tells browsers to use.
Files that should never be public, like a backup or a settings file.
Which WordPress and plugin versions your site shows to anyone who looks.
A secret key left in a page's public code.
Your login page: whether anything obvious is wrong.

body.paragraph: I'll say, in plain words: here's the door, here's how I'd get in, and here's how to shut it. The most important first.

A clean report doesn't mean a site is safe. It means I looked at these things, from the outside, and found nothing. Nothing I do replaces keeping your site updated, using strong sign-in, and asking someone you trust when you're unsure.
If a rule above isn't one you'd want from someone checking your site, tell me and I'll change it before I build anything. You can write to hello@superintelligenthacker.com.
To tell me to stay away, or to report something I did, write to security@superintelligenthacker.com.

body.paragraph: I only visit a site when its owner has asked me to check it, and has proved the site is theirs. I read what any visitor could read, one request at a time, and I never try passwords or break anything. The full list is on what I check, and what I never do.

props.lead: These are the rules for using Super Intelligent Hacker. By creating an account or using the check you agree to them. If you don't, please don't use it. Questions: hello@superintelligenthacker.com.

body.paragraph: Super Intelligent Hacker checks your own website the way someone trying to get in would, then tells you in plain words how to shut each door. It's run by Seth Shoultes in the United States. How it handles information is on the privacy page. The check is coming; it isn't running yet.

You must be at least 13, and old enough to agree to these terms where you live. Use a real email address and keep your sign-in safe. Only ask for a check of a site you own or have the right to change. You'll prove you control it before anything is checked.

body.subheading: What I do and don't do
body.paragraph: What the check looks at, and what it will never do, is on the page What I check, and what I never do. That page is part of these terms.

Break the law, or use the check to harm, harass or mislead people. Try to get into accounts, sites or systems that aren't yours, or to overload or break the service. Copy, resell or reverse-engineer it, except where the law lets you. If you do, we may stop your access.
The check works with other companies, such as Cloudflare, Resend and the sign-in providers. Their services come with their own terms. The ones that handle your information are on the privacy page.

You can stop using the check at any time and delete your reports. To have your account deleted, email hello@superintelligenthacker.com. We may suspend or end an account that breaks these terms, or if we have to stop running the check, and we'll give notice where we can.

The check is provided as it is. We work hard to keep it running and correct, but we don't promise it will always be available, error-free or fit for a particular purpose. A clean report isn't a promise that your site is safe: it shows what was found, from the outside, at one moment. To the most the law allows, we're not liable for lost profits, lost data or indirect damage, and our total liability for anything arising from the check is limited to what you paid us in the 12 months before the problem. Nothing here limits a right you have by law that can't be limited.

We may change these terms. When we do, we change this page and the date at the top, and by using the check after that you accept the new terms. These terms are governed by the laws of the State of Utah, United States, and a dispute is for the courts of that state.

pages.title: Privacy
pages.description: This page says what Super Intelligent Hacker keeps about you and your reports, which companies help us run it, and how to have it deleted.

props.heading: Privacy
props.lead: This page says what Super Intelligent Hacker keeps about you and your reports, which companies help us run it, and how to have it deleted. It covers this website and the check.

body.paragraph: The check is coming; this page says what we've decided before it runs.

Super Intelligent Hacker is run by Seth Shoultes in the United States. We don't sell your information, and we don't use it to show you ads. Questions about any of this: hello@superintelligenthacker.com.

Your account: your email address, through Key's sign-in. The site you've proved is yours, and the record that you proved it. That record is kept while the site stays verified, and deleted 30 days after you remove it or the proof stops working. Your reports: only you can open them. A key found in a public page is reported as its fixed beginning (like "sk_live_"), its length and where it was. Nothing after that beginning is ever stored or shown.

body.subheading: Companies that help us run it
body.paragraph: Cloudflare runs this website. Every request passes through it, so it sees your internet address and browser details.
Key signs you in. Its own privacy page says what it keeps.
Resend sends the sign-in emails, through Key. It receives your email address and the sign-in link or code.
The check never stores your internet address. To stop overuse it keeps short-lived counters that reset every hour, the way Key counts blocked sign-ins.
This website sets none.
The check is for people who run websites. It isn't meant for anyone under 13.
A report is kept for 30 days, then deleted. You can delete a report yourself at any time.
Logs of the requests a check makes (which pages, never their content) age out in 30 days.

You can delete a report any time, and it's gone. To have your whole account deleted, or to ask for a copy of what we hold about you, email hello@superintelligenthacker.com from that account's address. We reply and act within 30 days.
Companies in the list above keep their own records under their own privacy terms. Deleting your account with us does not reach into theirs, so ask them too if you want that.
